prompt_text:
Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that starts a streaming recognizer with language and punctuation settings using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 2 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 3 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 4 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 5 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 6 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import asyncio
from deepgram import (
    DeepgramClient,
    DeepgramClientOptions,
    LiveTranscriptionEvents,
    LiveOptions,
)

# You can replace this with your actual audio source
# For demonstration, we'll use a dummy generator
async def get_audio_stream():
    """Simulates an audio stream."""
    # In a real application, this would read from a microphone, file, etc.
    # For now, we yield empty bytes to keep the connection alive for a short period
    # and then close it.
    for _ in range(5):
        yield b''
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    print("Simulated audio stream ended.")

async def main():
    DEEPGRAM_API_KEY = os.getenv("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY")
    if not DEEPGRAM_API_KEY:
        raise ValueError("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

    # Configure Deepgram Client
    config: DeepgramClientOptions = DeepgramClientOptions(
        verbose=1,
    )
    deepgram = DeepgramClient(DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, config)

    # Establish a live transcription connection
    dg_connection = deepgram.listen.live.v("1")

    # Define event handlers
    def on_message(self, result, **kwargs):
        # The result object contains various details about the transcription
        # For a simple text output, we can access result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript
        if result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript:
            print(f"Deepgram result: {result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript}")

    def on_metadata(self, metadata, **kwargs):
        # Metadata contains information about the audio stream, such as channels, duration, etc.
        print(f"Deepgram metadata: {metadata}")

    def on_speech_started(self, speech_started, **kwargs):
        # Event triggered when speech is detected
        print(f"Deepgram speech started: {speech_started}")

    def on_error(self, error, **kwargs):
        # Event triggered on error
        print(f"Deepgram error: {error}")

    def on_close(self, close, **kwargs):
        # Event triggered when the connection closes
        print(f"Deepgram connection closed: {close}")

    # Register event handlers
    dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Transcript, on_message)
    dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Metadata, on_metadata)
    dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.SpeechStarted, on_speech_started)
    dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Error, on_error)
    dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Close, on_close)

    # Open the connection
    print("Attempting to open Deepgram connection...")
    await dg_connection.start(LiveOptions(
        language="en-US",
        punctuate=True,
        interim_results=False, # Set to True to get results before a full utterance is complete
        encoding="linear16",    # Specifies the audio encoding
        sample_rate=16000       # Specifies the sample rate of the audio
    ))
    print("Deepgram connection opened.")

    # Simulate sending audio data
    try:
        async for chunk in get_audio_stream():
            await dg_connection.send(chunk)
            # In a real scenario, you'd send actual audio bytes here
            # print(f"Sent {len(chunk)} bytes.")
    finally:
        # Close the connection when done sending audio
        print("Closing Deepgram connection...")
        await dg_connection.finish()
        print("Deepgram connection finished.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
